How long does a standard order take?

Do you remove and reinstall curtains?

Stain removal is not guaranteed. Fabric, stain age and prior treatment affect the result. The team explains visible concerns and works on a best-effort basis.

How do I pay?

blog.title: Garment Care Journal
blog.intro: Practical guidance from the Hangers counter: stains, storage, curtains, footwear and the small decisions that can prevent permanent damage.

items.t: What to check before curtains come down
items.s: Photograph the original fall, inspect weak stitching and note the lining. Fabric, sun exposure and prior shrinkage all affect the appropriate cleaning process. Hangers offers free curtain removal and reinstallation, with a typical turnaround of 6-7 days.
Heavy work needs breathable storage, supported folds and protection from humidity. Avoid direct contact with plastic for long periods, and address stains before storage.
The label helps identify fibre content and the manufacturer's intended process, but construction and embellishment still need inspection. Service decisions are made item by item.
Direct sun can yellow some materials and distort adhesives. Use shade and airflow, and avoid aggressive brushing on delicate finishes. Material determines the safe cleaning method.
Clean before storing, dry fully, fold without compressing, and use a breathable storage cover away from damp walls. Residue and moisture cause more storage damage than wear.

items.t: What to Do Before a Stain Reaches the Counter
items.s: Blot rather than rub, avoid heat, and tell the team what caused the stain. Home treatment can set some stains permanently — the safest first step is often to stop and ask.

note.h: Have an item you are not sure about?
note.p: Send a clear photo of the fabric, label or stain before attempting a home treatment.

privacy-policy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy-policy.intro: A plain-language explanation of the customer and order information Hangers uses to provide dry cleaning, local pickup and delivery, payment reconciliation and support. Last updated: 29 September 2026
sections: Our approach

Hangers Clothes Spa uses information entrusted to us to arrange and perform garment-care services, communicate about orders and payments, and operate this website. This notice describes the information used in those activities and the choices available to you. Razorpay processes online payment details under its own terms and privacy notice.
Information you provide

When you contact us, request a pickup, or place an order, we may receive your name, mobile number, email address, pickup or delivery address, requested services, preferred collection time, item and care details, order history, messages and support queries. We use payment references and transaction status to match a payment to an invoice; online payment credentials are entered into Razorpay’s checkout, not requested in our pickup form.
How we use it

Confirm service-area coverage and contact you about pickup scheduling. Identify items and orders, record inspection and service progress, and arrange return delivery. Issue invoices and receipts, reconcile payments, and investigate payment or service questions. Send relevant service and order updates through the contact channel used for your order. Protect the website and our records, prevent misuse, maintain operational accounts, and meet applicable record-keeping obligations. Understand public website usage and improve pages using Google Analytics and Google Tag Manager.
When information is shared

We share only information needed for the relevant task with service providers that support our operations. These may include Razorpay for payment processing, website and cloud hosting providers, and communication providers used to send customer updates. A provider may process information under its own privacy terms. We do not publish customer order details as public website content. We may also disclose records where required by law or to investigate fraud, security incidents or a customer dispute.
Website measurement and device information

The public website loads Google Analytics and Google Tag Manager on its marketing domain. Those services may receive technical and page-usage information such as pages viewed, browser/device signals and approximate network-derived information according to Google’s settings and policies. Your browser also stores limited session data when you use features such as pickup verification. You can use browser controls to limit cookies or storage; some site functions may then not work as intended.
Retention and security

We keep order, service, payment and customer-contact records for as long as they are needed to provide services, answer questions, reconcile accounts, address disputes, meet legal/accounting duties, and protect the business. Retention can therefore depend on the record and the reason it was created. We use access controls and operational safeguards, but no internet transmission or storage method can be promised to be completely risk-free.
Your requests and contact

You may contact us to ask what customer information relates to your order, correct inaccurate contact details, or raise a privacy concern. We may need to verify that you are the customer before changing or disclosing an order record. Some transaction records may need to be retained for accounting, legal or dispute-resolution purposes.
Updates to this notice
We may revise this notice when our website, service providers or practices change. The update date at the top of the page indicates the current published version.

blog:why-the-care-label-matters.title: Why the Care Label Matters
blog:why-the-care-label-matters.intro: The label helps identify fibre content and the manufacturer's intended process, but construction and embellishment still need inspection. Service decisions are made item by item.

image.alt: Checking a garment care label before cleaning

sections: What the label tells you
A care label states the fibre content and the manufacturer's recommended cleaning method — a genuinely useful starting point for how a garment should be handled.
Common symbols, plainly explained

A circle usually means dry clean, a crossed-out circle means do not dry clean, a tub means machine or hand wash, and dots inside a triangle or iron symbol indicate heat limits. These symbols exist precisely because fibre content alone does not tell the whole story of how a garment should be treated.
What the label does not tell you

A label cannot account for embellishment, lining, structural interfacing, or how a garment has already worn and been cared for. Two items with an identical label can still need different handling once construction and condition are inspected.
When labels are missing or faded

Older garments, altered items or pieces bought secondhand sometimes arrive without a readable label. In that case, fibre and construction are assessed directly — checking weave, weight, trims and any visible wear — rather than guessing from appearance alone.
Service decisions are made item by item

This is why every item is assessed individually before cleaning begins, rather than sorted purely by label. If a concern comes up — a delicate trim, a loose button, a prior repair — it is confirmed with you before work starts.
faq: What does a crossed-out dry clean symbol mean?
It means the garment should not be dry cleaned, usually because a trim, coating or fibre would react badly to dry-cleaning solvents. It is treated as a genuine warning, not a suggestion.
What happens if a garment has no care label?
The fabric, construction and condition are inspected directly to decide on a safe process, and any uncertainty is confirmed with you before cleaning begins.

image.alt: Professional dry cleaning process at Hangers Clothes Spa

sections: What dry cleaning actually is

Dry cleaning uses a liquid solvent instead of water to lift oils, body fats and embedded grime out of fabric. Because the solvent contains no water, fibres do not swell or change shape during the cycle, which is exactly why it suits garments that a normal wash would distort.
Why the process is gentler than it sounds

Professional machines move garments through the solvent with controlled agitation rather than the harsher mechanical action of a standard wash cycle. The goal is even saturation without abrasion, so fabric integrity holds up over repeated cleans rather than degrading with each one.
Inspection comes before cleaning

Every item is checked for its fibre content, construction and any existing damage before it goes anywhere near a machine. A loose button, a delicate trim or a prior repair is flagged and, where it matters, confirmed with you before work starts, rather than discovered after the fact.
The solvent itself is filtered and reused

Professional dry-cleaning solvent is distilled and filtered between cycles so each batch is cleaned in genuinely purified solvent, not contaminated with residue from the last load. This is part of why the process stays consistent order after order.
Collected from Mulund, processed at Mulund West

Every dry-cleaning order — regardless of which served area it's collected from — is brought to the same Mulund West facility and goes through the same process and quality checks. Standard turnaround is 4-5 days.
What is not sent for standard dry cleaning

Some fabrics or embellishments need a different approach entirely, which is why every item is assessed individually rather than processed on assumption. If something needs a different treatment, that is confirmed with you rather than pushed through the standard process anyway.
faq: How long does dry cleaning take?
Standard turnaround is 4-5 days from collection to delivery.
Is dry cleaning safe for all fabrics?

Most fabrics suited to dry cleaning benefit from the solvent-based process, but every item is inspected individually first — construction and condition, not just fabric type, determine the right approach.
